title: Say it. Snap it. Show it.
subtitle: A short tour of Workbench

slides.title: Say it. Snap it. Show it.
slides.narration: This is a quick tour of Workbench: a set of small tools that sit on top of every app on my Mac. Say it, snap it, show it.

slides.title: Talk, and it types where you are.
slides.narration: This is Dictate. I press Option V wherever I'm typing, say what I mean, and the words land right there. If I lose track of it, the same text is waiting in History.

slides.title: Leave every call with the words.
slides.narration: Here's a call that's just finished. I started it once at the beginning and didn't touch it again. One click on Copy transcript and every word is on my clipboard, ready for the follow-up.

slides.title: Snap a few screens. Talk. Get a deck.
slides.narration: This is a Snap & Talk session: each screenshot keeps what I said beside it, so the assistant knows what matters. When the order's right, I hand it off and the assistant builds the deck.

slides.title: Mark it up mid-demo.
slides.narration: When I'm presenting I hold Option D, draw over whatever's on screen, then let go and carry on. Option X clears it.

slides.title: Nothing gets lost.
slides.narration: And nothing gets lost. Every dictation, meeting, Snap and result lands in History on this Mac, newest first, and I can search all of it.
